title: Ya-Sin 1 to 4: the opening letters and their rules: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ya-Sin 1 to 4 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 12. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: A Hafs detail: يسٓ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ
points: In Hafs: izhar, a clear noon

keywords.def: a madd after a hamza: 2 counts
reciting each letter with its right and its rules

questions.q: Read 36:1 to 4 joined, then stopping at each ayah, keeping your 'arid length.
questions.a: Joined: yaa-seen wal-qur'aanil-hakeem ...; stopping: ٱلْحَكِيمْ, ٱلْمُرْسَلِينْ, مُّسْتَقِيمْ with a consistent 'arid.

questions.q: Breakout pairs: recite Juz' 'Amma block 1 (78 to 80) to a partner, then 36:1 to 4. Today's rota group recites 36:1 to 4 to the teacher.
questions.a: Partner rubric and one target; teacher records rota scores.

questions.q: Extend: find two other surahs that open with letters and read them.
Stretch: why is the alif in «ٱلْقُرْءَانِ» only 2 counts though a hamza is near?
questions.a: The hamza comes before the madd letter (madd badal), not after it, so it stays 2.
A) yaa-seeen: ya 2, seen 6. Opening letters are read by their names; سين has madd lazim harfi (6).

questions.q: The noon of «يسٓ» before «وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ» in Hafs is ...
Think again: Some surahs open with letters like الٓمٓ, يسٓ, قٓ. Nobody reads them as words. How are they read?
questions.a: By their letter names: yaa, seen; each name follows madd rules (2 or 6 counts).
